complete_examples.text: Besides, the matrix coupling method in Ref. [30] is employed to construct the vehicle-rail coupled dynamic equations based on the nonlinear Hertz contact theory and nonlinear saturated creep theory [2,28,29].

A key point is the coupled method of the train sub-model and the track structure sub-model, a matrix coupled method [4] is proposed by Xu to characterize the interaction of the wheelset and rail based on the nonlinear Hertz contact theory [3] and modified saturated creep theory [30].

The coupling of vehicle and track is implemented by the wheel-rail contact model, which is depicted by the nonlinear Hertz contact theory (Zhai 2015) and Kalker linear creep theory (Kalker 1991), respectively.

In this work, the trace line method is used to determine the geometric rela tionship between the wheel and rail, the normal force of the wheel-rail contact is obtained by the nonlinear Hertz contact theory (Zhai, 2015), and the modified saturated creep theory is employed to calculate the tangential force (Shen et al., 1983; Zhai, 2015).
For instance, Zhai [13] proposed the vehicle-track coupling dynamic method, where the normal contact forces are calculated by the nonlinear Hertz contact theory.

In this model, the track line method is utilized to characterize the geometric relationship between the wheelset and rail, the normal con tact force is determined by the nonlinear Hertz contact theory [13] and the tangential forces are obtained by the modified saturation creep theory [33].

Their geometric relationship is deter mined by the trace line method, the normal contact forces are calculated by the nonlinear Hertz contact theory [20] and the corre sponding tangential forces are obtained by the modified saturated creep theory [20,53].
